subject: Request: Temporary SLA Carveout for Rate Caps — Novaera Health
messages:
From: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Rate caps causing production errors during morning batch jobs

Hi Alex —

Quick note from our infra team: the scheduled morning inference batches (07:00–09:00 PST) have been hitting Redwood's rate caps over the last three days and we're seeing elevated 429s and occasional tail latency spikes. This is directly affecting our triage pipeline and downstream SLAs with providers.

Can Redwood provide a temporary carveout or a higher burst window for these time slots while we rework batching on our side? We can share telemetry and a short list of request patterns. Ideally we'd like to avoid any contract-level changes but need assurance we won't see a repeat next week.

Attaching a brief request form with the peak times and traffic shape.

Cheers,
Emma Cortez
Senior Platform Engineer, Novaera Health
[Attachment: novaera-ratecap-request-form.pdf (pdf)]

From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T10:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Rate caps causing production errors during morning batch jobs

Thanks for the details, Emma — really helpful.

Short answer: we can offer a temporary rate-cap carveout for scheduled batch windows, but we need to coordinate with CS and Legal to scope the duration and guardrails. Monica, can you take point on operational constraints (burst size, per-token limits) and work with Novaera on telemetry ingestion? Markus, FYI — we may need a one-page amendment for a time-boxed SLA exception.

Emma — can you confirm the exact recurring windows (local times) and an estimated QPS and token-per-request distribution? That'll let us propose specific burst limits and a short mitigation plan.

I included a proposed next step in the attachment: an ops checklist and the minimal amendment template.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0134
[Attachment: redwood-temporary-sla-draft-20261120.docx]

From: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@novaera.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:28:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Rate caps causing production errors during morning batch jobs

Thanks Alex —

Confirmed windows: Mon–Fri 07:00–09:00 PST, and a smaller evening spike 18:30–19:00 PST. Peak measured QPS ~420 (bursting to ~2k sustained for ~3–4 minutes during warm-up). Median token/request ~120; heavy tails up to 1,200 for some analysis jobs.

We're comfortable with a time-boxed carveout for two weeks while we roll batching changes, but need guarantees that fallback routing or throttling won't silently drop requests. For commercial certainty, our procurement lead (Rajiv) needs a documented temporary SLA with a clear rollback date and failure remediation path.

Attaching the telemetry excerpt.

—Emma
[Attachment: novaera-telemetry-excerpt.csv (csv)]

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:10:00-05:00
Subject: Proposed operational carveout: details and guardrails

Hi all —

Thanks for the telemetry, Emma. Based on the numbers we've proposed the following temporary carveout:
- Window: Mon–Fri 07:00–09:00 PST + Mon–Fri 18:30–19:00 PST
- Duration: 14 days (starting 2026-11-24 07:00 PST)
- Burst allowance: up to 2,500 QPS for 5-minute rolling windows during the morning warm-up, with a sustained cap of 600 QPS outside short bursts
- Token soft-limit: no hard drops under 200 tokens; requests above 200 tokens are subject to fair-share queuing during high contention
- Observability: streaming metrics to Novaera's shared telemetry endpoint + RW alerting to on-call

Conditions:
1) Novaera will enable prefix/KV caching on the heaviest pipelines within 48 hours of start date.
2) Redwood will monitor for error-rate regressions and reserve the right to revert to standard caps if system-wide fairness is degraded. Any revert will be communicated with 30 minutes notice.

Markus — please advise on a minimal contractual amendment (one page) that captures duration, guardrails, and a liability cap. Emma/Rajiv — if these operational terms look acceptable I can draft the DocuSign for signatures.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@novaera.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Proposed operational carveout: details and guardrails

Monica — this looks reasonable. A few procurement asks before we sign:
- Can the duration be extended to three weeks if we find the batching rollout taking longer? We prefer an automatic 7-day extension option subject to mutual written consent.
- Please clarify the exact rollback triggers and whether any queued requests will be retried or failed with 5xx/4xx codes. Silent drops are unacceptable.
- Need an SLA uptime target for the carveout window (we'd like to record 99.9% availability for the carveout period, limited to Redwood's control plane and routing).

If you can add those points into the amendment we can route internally and push signature same day.

—Rajiv (Procurement, Novaera)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Cortez <emma@novaera.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@novaera.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Proposed operational carveout: details and guardrails

Folks —

We can accommodate the carveout and the extension option with the following legal-first guardrails to be included in the one-page amendment (attached):
- Duration: 14 days by default with a single mutual 7-day extension if requested in writing at least 48 hours before the default end date
- Rollback triggers: sustained system-wide fairness degradation (measured as >5% error-rate delta across impacted customers for >15 minutes) or detection of significant SLA regression affecting other tenants; rollback will be preceded by a 30-minute notice when feasible
- Queuing/retry behavior: Redwood will not silently drop in-window requests. Requests subject to fair-share queuing will be retried according to a documented retry policy; if requests ultimately fail they will surface standard 4xx/5xx statuses and be logged for Novaera review
- Uptime commitment for carveout window: Redwood will aim for 99.9% availability for control-plane routing and will apply pro-rated credits only for downtime due to Redwood's routing failures within the carveout window; credits limited to 10% of monthly invoice for the carveout period

I attached a draft amendment and a DocuSign envelope. Monica — please start the DocuSign flow once we have confirmation on the extension option language (Rajiv).

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-novaera-sla-amendment-20261124.pdf]
